  1. lem✓Lax793645.Counterexample

    A counterexample to Hadwiger's conjecture

    Theorem 1.1 asserts that graphs of arbitrarily large order mmm have independence number at most two and connected-matching number less than m/100m/100m/100. Together with Proposition 3.5, this gives graphs of arbitrarily large order with h(G)<χ(G)h(G)<\chi(G)h(G)<χ(G).

    The proof package establishes the existence assertion by the complete binary-frame construction, and derives the coloring consequences from it.

  5. defLax793645.Holes

    The hole relation

    Two endpoints form a hole when their witnesses have the same ambient image, their opposite functionals give the prescribed gradients, and their role bits differ.

    1import Lax793645.ConstructionData
    2
    … module docstring, 8 lines

    12namespace Lax793645.Holes

    14/-- The six-term cancellation uses only these evaluations. -/
    15def relation {I X V : Type*} (U : I → X → V) (u : I → V → ZMod 2)
    16 (role : X → ZMod 2) (T : X → X → ZMod 2) (i j : I) : Prop :=
    17 ∃ x y : X, U i x = U j y ∧
    18 (∀ z, u j (U i z) = role z + T x z) ∧
    19 (∀ z, u i (U j z) = role z + T y z) ∧
    20 role x + role y = 1
    21
    22/-- The relation on valid quadratic frames in the construction. -/
    23abbrev hole := @Lax793645.ConstructionData.Frames.oneHole
    24
    25end Lax793645.Holes

  6. lem✓Lax793645.TriangleFreeHoles

    Three holes cannot form a triangle

    The hole relation is symmetric and irreflexive. Evaluating its six functional identities around a triangle cancels the ambient evaluations and the symmetric bilinear terms. The three remaining role parities sum to one.

    18 (injective : ∀ i, Function.Injective (U i)) (symm : ∀ x y, T x y = T y x) :
    19 let H := Holes.relation U u a T
    20 (∀ i j, H i j → H j i) ∧ (∀ i, ¬H i i) ∧

  11. lem✓Lax793645.ClippedExposure

    The loss from revealing a matching edge

    Both marginals of the joint law are the same, and conflicting pairs have zero joint mass. On the part of the space satisfying the density cap, half the independent conflict probability, after the lowest threshold is subtracted, bounds the expected loss of the clipped potential.

    22
    23axiom dyadic_exposure_joint (q σ : Wgt X) (P : X → X → ℝ)
    24 (hq : IsLaw q) (hσ : IsLaw σ)
    25 (hP : ∀ y x, 0 ≤ P y x) (hrow : ∀ y, ∑ x, P y x = σ y)
    26 (hcol : ∀ x, ∑ y, P y x = σ x)
    27 (C : X → X → Prop) (hzero : ∀ y x, C y x → P y x = 0)
    28 (A : X → Prop) (γ κ : ℝ) (hγ : 0 ≤ γ)
    29 (b : ℕ) (hb : 0 < b) (hκ : κ ≤ (2:ℝ)^b*γ)
    30 (hcap : ∀ x, A x → σ x ≤ κ* q x) :
    31 (∑ x, σ x * ind (A x) * pr σ (fun y => C y x)) - γ ≤
    32 2*(clippedPotential q (fun i : Fin b => (2:ℝ)^i.val*γ) σ -
    33 avg σ (clippedPotential q (fun i : Fin b => (2:ℝ)^i.val*γ) ∘ posterior P σ))

  13. lem✓Lax793645.MatchingExposure

    From a conflict probability to a sampled graph

    Assume the conflict lower bound for every admissible edge law of a finite triangle-free hole relation. Sampling enough vertices gives a graph with independence number at most 2 and connected matching number less than m/100m/100m/100 for a graph of order mmm. The construction uses scale 2 in the general sampling estimate.

  21. lem✓Lax793645.AffinePointMatrices

    Symmetry and diagonal identities for affine points

    In one factor the affine point squares span exactly the symmetric matrices whose diagonal entries agree with their entries in the constant column. For sss and ttt with constant coordinate one, form the outer square of s⊗ts\otimes ts⊗t. Every linear combination of these squares is separately symmetric in the two indices of either factor and satisfies the affine diagonal identity in each factor.

  62. lem✓Lax793645.ScalarDuality

    Duality for the four scalar equations

    An insoluble scalar target has a linear functional that vanishes on every available generator and is nonzero on the target. Surjectivity on the base coordinates forces at least one of the four coupled weights to be nonzero.
